knowledge_point.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}20 \\ -65 \\ 15\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}20 \\ -65 \\ 15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 0 \\ x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}x_{2} \\ - 2 x_{2} \\ 2 x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3 x_{3} \\ - 11 x_{3} \\ x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}20 \\ -65 \\ 15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} \\ - 2 x_{2} - 11 x_{3} \\ x_{1} + 2 x_{2} + x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}20 \\ -65 \\ 15\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=20 \\ - 2 x_{2} - 11 x_{3} &=-65 \\ x_{1} + 2 x_{2} + x_{3} &=15\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 20 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -65 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 15\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 20 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -65 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 15\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 20 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -65 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-1)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 20 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & -65\end{array}\right] && R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 20 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -15 & -75\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(2)R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 20 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=\left(- \frac{1}{15}\right)R_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=20 \\ x_{2} - 2 x_{3} &=-5 \\ x_{3} &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=5.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+(-2)(5)=-5\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=5
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(1)(5)+(3)(5)=20\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=0
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=0$, $x_2=5$, $x_3=5$, which means

$$
0a_1+(5)a_2+(5)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(0)+(5)+(5)=10.
$$

generation.domain: fixed observed coefficient matrix; integer RHS; moderate integer solution coordinates in [-7,7], hard inconsistent b in [-9,9]^3

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 11 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}10 \\ 40 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 11 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}10 \\ 40 \\ -9\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 0 \\ 4 x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- 2 x_{2} \\ - 5 x_{2} \\ - x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3 x_{3} \\ 11 x_{3} \\ - 2 x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}10 \\ 40 \\ -9\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} - 2 x_{2} + 3 x_{3} \\ - 5 x_{2} + 11 x_{3} \\ 4 x_{1} - x_{2} - 2 x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}10 \\ 40 \\ -9\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - 2 x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=10 \\ - 5 x_{2} + 11 x_{3} &=40 \\ 4 x_{1} - x_{2} - 2 x_{3} &=-9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & 40 \\ 4 & -1 & -2 & -9\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & 40 \\ 4 & -1 & -2 & -9\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & 40 \\ 0 & 7 & -14 & -49\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-4)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & 7 & -14 & -49 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & 40\end{array}\right] && R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -7 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & 40\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{7}\right)R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 3 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(5)R_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - 2 x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=10 \\ x_{2} - 2 x_{3} &=-7 \\ x_{3} &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=5.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+(-2)(5)=-7\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=3
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(-2)(3)+(3)(5)=10\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=1
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=1$, $x_2=3$, $x_3=5$, which means

$$
1a_1+(3)a_2+(5)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(1)+(3)+(5)=9.
$$
